title: Serving a model: batch versus real time, cold starts, GPU versus CPU

claims.text: Serving large models at high throughput requires batching many requests at a time, and existing systems struggled because the key-value cache memory for each request is huge and grows and shrinks dynamically, being significantly wasted by fragmentation and redundant duplication when managed inefficiently, which limits the batch size.

source.title: Woosuk Kwon et al., Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention, Proceedings of the 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, 2023 (arXiv:2309.06180)

claims.text: Prior systems allocated a contiguous memory chunk sized to a request's maximum possible length, causing severe internal fragmentation when actual lengths are shorter, with the chunk remaining reserved for the request's lifetime.

source.title: Woosuk Kwon et al., Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention, Proceedings of the 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, 2023 (arXiv:2309.06180)

claims.text: The order-of-magnitude figures that decide placement: a main memory reference is around 100 nanoseconds, a round trip within the same datacenter around 500,000, a disk seek around 10,000,000. Moving work to another machine costs a datacenter round trip; loading state from disk costs a seek.

source.title: Jeffrey Dean, Large-Scale Distributed Systems at Google: Current Systems and Future Directions, keynote at LADIS 2009, October 2009 — the slide deck carrying Numbers Everyone Should Know

beats.broke: a model has to answer requests, and the hardware that runs it is expensive, slow to acquire and useless while idle — so the arrangement that gives the fastest single answer is rarely the one you can afford
beats.fix: decide by the shape of the demand rather than by the model: predictable bulk work runs as batches on saturated hardware, unpredictable interactive work needs capacity held ready, and the two have different economics
beats.cost: holding capacity ready is paying for idleness, and not holding it means the first request after a quiet period pays for loading everything — there is no arrangement that avoids both
beats.interview: when it is correct to serve a model on ordinary processors rather than accelerators
